newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks extend losses at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks extend losses at close.

text.p: Argentina's bolsa closed lower in quiet trading Wednesday, pressured by a downswing in U.S. stocks and bonds, dealers said.

"The market seems to be growing more volatile and players want to secure short-term gains, which is causing this slump," said analyst Maximiliano Goff at Rio Research. "However, this may be a good time to build up medium- and long-term positions because the underlying trend remains firm."
The blue-chip MerVal index shed 1.0 percent, slipping off a high of 688.53 to close at 679.47. It now stands narrowly lower on the week.

Volume in the session was paltry, with 18.4 million pesos traded on the floor compared to an already modest tally of 23.6 million Tuesday and over-the-counter deals of 60.2 million pesos against 100.1 million Tuesday.
"When prices drop, volume shrinks. That's a good sign because it shows the downside is limited," said a trader at a leading local brokerage.
Analysts predicted the MerVal might stay trapped in a range of 680-700 in the near term as international interest rate jitters mount ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting February 4-5.
"We could be heading for some erratic swings on Wall Street which will temporarily offset the confidence derived from (Tuesday's $2.0 billion) global bond deal," Goff said.
The broad market index closed off 0.8 percent, with losers outpacing winners 37 to 22 and 14 issues closing flat.

Only main-tier risers were pulp maker Celulosa, holding firm Comercial del Plata and real estate developer Irsa, up 1.6 percent, 1.5 percent and 0.9 percent, respectively. Losers were led by oil company Astra, off 2.6 percent, and steelmaker Acindar and construction stock Polledo, both off 1.9 percent.
